questions.q: Which is NOT one of the three things a plaintiff must prove in negligence?
choices: The defendant owed them a duty of care
The defendant intended to cause the harm
The defendant breached the standard of care
The damage that resulted wasn't too remote
questions.explain: Negligence is about carelessness, not intent. The plaintiff proves duty, breach and damage that isn't too remote.

questions.q: What standard of care are licensees held to?
choices: Perfection in every single transaction
What a competent real estate professional would do
What an average member of the public would do
Whatever the client personally expected of them
questions.explain: Licensees are judged against a competent real estate professional. Courts set it close to, but not at, perfection.

questions.q: A listing says "information believed accurate but not guaranteed" and the square footage is wrong. What did Koerber v. Salmon decide?
choices: The disclaimer fully protected the seller's licensee
The general disclaimer didn't defeat the buyer's claim
Square footage errors can never ground a claim
Only the seller can ever be liable for listing errors
questions.explain: A general disclaimer was ineffective. Specific disclaimers work better, and none protect a licensee who knows the information is wrong.

questions.q: A buyer's agent can't verify the seller's figures. What's the best advice?
choices: Tell the buyer the figures are probably fine to rely on
Send the buyer to experts and consider a subject clause
Refuse to show the property to the buyer at all
Have the seller sign a statutory declaration instead
questions.explain: Send the buyer to qualified professionals, and consider a subject that shifts the risk of inaccuracy to the seller.

questions.q: When is a brokerage vicariously liable for a licensee's wrongful act?
choices: Only if the managing broker approved the act first
When it happens in the ordinary course of their work
Only for careless acts, and never for deliberate fraud
Whenever the licensee is licensed with that brokerage
questions.explain: Vicarious liability covers acts in the ordinary course of work, even fraud. Courts treat representatives like employees.

questions.q: What is the most common basis of liability against licensees?
choices: Breach of fiduciary duty
Misrepresentation
Errors in drafting
Trespass to land
questions.explain: Misrepresentation, negligent or fraudulent, is the most common basis of liability.
questions.ref: Lesson 6 · Part 1: How licensees get sued

questions.q: Which is one of the five requirements for negligent misrepresentation under Queen v. Cognos?
choices: The defendant intended to deceive the plaintiff
The plaintiff reasonably relied on the statement
The statement was made in a signed document
The plaintiff paid a fee for the advice given
questions.explain: The five are: special relationship, untrue statement, negligence, reasonable reliance and resulting damage. Intent isn't required.

questions.q: How does deceit differ from negligent misrepresentation?
choices: Deceit requires the statement to be made in writing
Deceit is a knowing or reckless falsehood, by anyone
Deceit only applies to licensees and other experts
Deceit doesn't allow the victim to recover damages
questions.explain: Deceit is moral fraud: knowingly or recklessly false. Unlike negligent misrepresentation, the speaker needn't be an expert.

questions.q: A seller tells you the lot dimensions; you haven't measured. What's the prudent way to pass them on?
choices: Verbally, presented as a confirmed fact
In writing, stating where the figures came from
Don't mention the dimensions to anyone at all
Round them up by 5% as a safety margin
questions.explain: Information not from your own direct knowledge should be given in writing with its source.

questions.q: Under Rules ss.49–50, what must accompany a promise like "I'll sell your property for $500,000 in 3 weeks"?
choices: Nothing extra, as long as the promise is honest
A signed written statement giving all the details
Approval from BCFSA before the promise is made
A refundable deposit paid by the licensee
questions.explain: Inducement promises are allowed only with a signed written statement giving all the details. A licensee was disciplined over an undocumented $500 inspection promise.

questions.q: In Russell v. Wispinski, why were the licensees found negligent?
choices: They lost the buyer's deposit cheque before closing
A vague amendment became a counter-offer and the deal died
They failed to register the transfer on time
They didn't disclose a conflict of interest to the seller
questions.explain: Unclear drafting turned an amendment into a counter-offer the buyer could reject. Clear drafting would have closed the deal.

questions.q: In Ocean City Realty v. A & M Holdings, what happened to the commission?
choices: It was cut in half as a penalty
The brokerage lost all of it
It was paid to the buyer instead
It was held in trust for a hearing
questions.explain: Secretly agreeing to split commission with the buyer, without telling the seller, cost the brokerage its whole commission.

questions.q: When a client alleges breach of fiduciary duty, who has to prove what?
choices: The client must prove every breach beyond doubt
The agent must show they fulfilled their duties
BCFSA must investigate before any lawsuit starts
Neither side; the judge decides on overall fairness
questions.explain: Unusually, the burden is on the agent to show they properly discharged their fiduciary duties.

questions.q: What can a real estate board do to a member who breaches the REALTOR® Code?
choices: Suspend the member's real estate licence
Expel them, which cuts off MLS® access
Refer them for a criminal prosecution
Cancel their brokerage's licence
questions.explain: Boards can reprimand, fine, suspend or expel members, but can't touch the licence. Expulsion ends MLS® access.
questions.ref: Lesson 6 · Part 1: How licensees get sued

questions.q: Which statement about money laundering through real estate is correct?
choices: It almost always involves suitcases of cash
Most dirty money is already in the system before the deal
It's only a concern for residential property sales
It can't happen if a bank mortgage is involved in the deal
questions.explain: "Bags of cash" is a myth. Most laundered money arrives electronically or through other instruments.
questions.ref: Lesson 6 · What it is and why real estate attracts it

questions.q: In what order do the three stages of money laundering happen?
choices: Layering, placement, integration
Placement, layering, integration
Integration, placement, layering
Placement, integration, layering
questions.explain: Placement (into the system), layering (hide the trail), integration (bring back as legitimate).

questions.q: A criminal pays tradespeople in cash to renovate, then sells the house at a big gain. Which stage is this mainly?
choices: Placement
Integration
Smurfing
Structuring
questions.explain: Renovating with dirty money and selling creates apparently legitimate profit: integration.

questions.q: Which licensee is NOT a reporting entity under the PCMLTFA?
choices: A representative helping a buyer purchase a condo
A licensee providing only rental property management
A managing broker of a trading services brokerage
An associate broker listing a warehouse for sale
questions.explain: Only licensees acting in the purchase or sale of real estate are reporting entities. Pure rental or strata managers aren't.

questions.q: Which is one of the five required parts of a brokerage compliance program?
choices: An outside audit at least every five years
A documented risk assessment
Approval of the program by FINTRAC itself
A dedicated, full-time compliance officer
questions.explain: The five: compliance officer, written policies, documented risk assessment, written training, and a review every 2 years. The officer can be the managing broker.

questions.q: What counts as a large cash transaction?
choices: $5,000 or more in any single payment
$10,000 or more at once, or in total within 24 hours
$10,000 or more received within one calendar month
Any cash payment at all, regardless of the amount
questions.explain: $10,000+ in a single transaction or multiple payments within 24 hours from or for the same person.

questions.q: Which way of verifying a client's photo ID is NOT permitted?
choices: Viewing the original ID in person
Viewing the ID over a video call
Authenticating it with approved software
Comparing it to the person presenting it
questions.explain: Video-call viewing and photocopies aren't allowed. Remote checks need software that authenticates security features.

questions.q: Using the credit file method, how old must the client's Canadian credit file be?
choices: At least 6 months
At least 3 years
At least 1 year
At least 5 years
questions.explain: The credit file must be Canadian and have existed for at least 3 years.

questions.q: For FINTRAC purposes, who is a beneficial owner?
choices: Anyone who owns or controls 10% or more
Anyone who owns or controls 25% or more
Only the shareholders named in the register
Only the directors and senior officers
questions.explain: 25% or more, directly or indirectly. LOTA uses 10% for corporate interest holders.

questions.q: Rochelle owns 90% of HoldCo, which owns 90% of PropCo. What's her indirect interest in PropCo?
questions.explain: 90% × 90% = 81%, well above 25%, so she's a beneficial owner of PropCo.

questions.q: Besides the start of a business relationship, when must you check whether someone is a PEP or HIO?
choices: When they pay a deposit of more than $25,000
When you receive $100,000+ in cash or virtual currency
Only if they ordinarily live outside of Canada
Only when you're filing a suspicious transaction report
questions.explain: Receiving $100,000+ in cash or virtual currency also triggers the PEP/HIO determination.

questions.q: When must a Large Cash Transaction Report be filed?
choices: Within 30 days of the transaction
Within 15 calendar days of it
Within 24 hours of the transaction
By the end of the calendar year
questions.explain: Within 15 calendar days. Many brokerages refuse cash to avoid the obligation.

questions.q: What's the dollar threshold for filing a suspicious transaction report?
choices: There's none
questions.explain: STRs have no monetary threshold, and they cover attempted transactions too.

questions.q: What standard triggers the obligation to file an STR?
choices: A gut feeling or hunch
Reasonable grounds to suspect
Reasonable grounds to believe
Proof beyond a reasonable doubt
questions.explain: Reasonable grounds to suspect: a possibility, for reasons another trained person would likely share. You don't need proof.

questions.q: Having filed an STR, what must you NOT do?
choices: Discuss it with your compliance officer
Tip off the client in a way that may harm a probe
Keep a copy of the report on the client's file
Continue monitoring the client's account activity
questions.explain: Tipping off is prohibited. Talking with your compliance officer or managing broker is fine.

questions.q: Which is a recognized money-laundering red flag?
choices: The buyer's spouse pays the deposit
An unrelated third party pays the deposit
The buyer asks for a home inspection
The buyer gets a mortgage from a major bank
questions.explain: A third-party deposit (other than a spouse or parent) is a listed indicator.

questions.q: How long must PCMLTFA records generally be kept?
choices: 2 years
5 years
7 years
10 years
questions.explain: At least 5 years, and producible to FINTRAC within 30 days of a request.

questions.q: What's the maximum FINTRAC administrative penalty per violation for an entity such as a brokerage?
choices: $2 million
questions.explain: $500,000 for entities and $100,000 for individuals, and all are published. Criminal penalties reach $2M and/or 5 years.

questions.q: Who prepares and files LOTA transparency declarations and reports?
choices: The listing licensee
The client's lawyer or notary
The buyer's mortgage lender
BCFSA licensing staff
questions.explain: Licensees don't file them, and shouldn't advise on LOTA. Refer clients to lawyers or notaries.

questions.q: Which is true of the Land Owner Transparency Registry?
choices: It confirms legal ownership, like the title register
It's separate from title and doesn't confirm ownership
It can only be searched by law enforcement agencies
It replaces the need for a title search by licensees
questions.explain: LOTR is separate from the Land Title Act register, isn't verified by anyone but the filer, and doesn't confirm ownership.

questions.q: Which is good advice to a seller client given climate-related risks?
choices: Cancel the insurance once the contract is signed
Keep insurance in place until completion
Remove any s.219 covenants before listing
Avoid mentioning known hazards to buyers
questions.explain: If the deal collapses, the seller still needs coverage. Keep insurance until completion.

questions.q: What is conduct unbecoming a licensee?
choices: Any technical breach of a specific Rule, however minor it is
Conduct harming the public interest or trust in the industry
A minor paperwork error later fixed by an undertaking
Only misconduct by a licensee during a live transaction
questions.explain: It's about public interest, confidence and the industry's reputation, and can include conduct outside work.
questions.ref: Lesson 6 · Conduct unbecoming reaches your private life

questions.q: What is the "headline test"?
choices: Checking that a listing headline is accurate
Imagining your decision reported as news
Asking BCFSA to review a decision in advance
Comparing your ad headlines with competitors'
questions.explain: If you'd be embarrassed to see it as a headline or viral post, it probably fails honesty and integrity.

questions.q: How long does the duty of confidentiality to a client last?
choices: Until completion of the transaction
Indefinitely, even after the relationship ends
For 7 years, the same as brokerage records
Until the client lists with another brokerage
questions.explain: Confidentiality, unlike most fiduciary duties, survives the end of the relationship.
questions.ref: Lesson 6 · Rules s.30: your duties to clients

questions.q: A seller said they won't accept anything below list. An offer arrives below list. What should you do?
choices: Reject it on the seller's behalf without presenting it
Present it, unless told otherwise (ideally in writing)
Ask the buyer to raise it before you present it
Hold it until a better offer comes along
questions.explain: Rules s.30(g): communicate all offers promptly unless instructed otherwise. A below-list offer may still lead to a counter-offer.
questions.ref: Lesson 6 · Rules s.30: your duties to clients

questions.q: What does a licensee need before signing an agreement on a client's behalf?
choices: Verbal permission from the client
Written authorization from the client
The managing broker's approval only
Nothing, if the terms are standard
questions.explain: Rules s.45 requires written authorization to sign for a client.
questions.ref: Lesson 6 · Rules s.30: your duties to clients

questions.q: How must a conflict of interest be disclosed to a client?
choices: Verbally, at any point before completion
Promptly, fully, in writing, and separately
In a clause inside the service agreement
Only if the client asks about conflicts
questions.explain: Rules s.30(i)–(j): avoid conflicts; disclose promptly and fully in writing, separately from service and trade agreements.

questions.q: A licensee lent their buyer client $50,000 so the purchase could close. What was the outcome in 2024 BCSRE 1?
choices: No penalty, because the loan helped the client
A penalty and costs for an undisclosed conflict
Licence cancellation for a finding of fraud
A criminal charge laid under the PCMLTFA
questions.explain: $5,000 administrative penalty, $22,958.18 in expenses and two courses. Lending created an undisclosed conflict.

questions.q: After disclosing a conflict and getting the client's consent, can you always continue?
choices: Yes, the client's consent fully cures the conflict
No; if you can't serve the client loyally, you can't
Yes, as long as your managing broker approves it
Only in commercial, not residential, transactions
questions.explain: Disclosure and consent don't remove your duty to act in the client's best interests.

questions.q: Under Rules s.29, to whom must a representative report possible misconduct in their brokerage?
choices: The client involved
Their managing broker
The local real estate board
FINTRAC
questions.explain: Representatives and associate brokers must promptly notify their managing broker.
questions.ref: Lesson 6 · The duty to report misconduct

questions.q: When should a licensee go directly to BCFSA rather than their managing broker?
choices: Never; the managing broker must always hear it first
When the managing broker is the one at fault
Only after the client has filed a complaint
Only for misconduct at a different brokerage
questions.explain: Direct reporting is appropriate for urgent risks, an unavailable MB, concerns about the MB's handling, or misconduct by the MB.
questions.ref: Lesson 6 · The duty to report misconduct

questions.q: A managing broker arranges compensation for a client harmed by a licensee's misconduct. Does that end the duty to report?
choices: Yes, the matter has been resolved
No; compensation is a separate issue
Yes, if the client agrees in writing
Only if the amount is under $5,000
questions.explain: The decision to report is separate from compensation. Making it right with the client doesn't remove the obligation.
questions.ref: Lesson 6 · The duty to report misconduct

questions.q: What's the first step in the ethical decision-making framework?
choices: Make your choice and justify it to others
Consider the situation and the ethical issues
Identify the feasible alternatives open to you
Evaluate the alternatives against the Rules
questions.explain: 1 Consider the situation, 2 identify stakeholders, 3 list alternatives, 4 evaluate, 5 choose and justify.
questions.ref: Lesson 6 · The five-step ethical decision framework

questions.q: What do you owe a buyer who is not your client?
choices: Nothing; you owe duties only to your own client
Honesty and reasonable care, but not fiduciary loyalty
The same fiduciary duties you owe your own client
Only the duties listed in the PCMLTFA
questions.explain: No fiduciary duty to third parties, but you must be honest, take reasonable care and avoid conduct unbecoming.

questions.q: How does BCFSA judge whether a licensee acted "reasonably" under s.34?
choices: By what the client felt was reasonable at the time
Against a competent licensee, e.g. a panel of managing brokers
By whether the licensee followed their own usual habits
Only by whether a court has already found them negligent
questions.explain: The test is a competent licensee's standard; think of a reasonable informed third party or a panel of five managing brokers.
